name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Scatterfield SF-2 'Hornets Nest'
description:
An electromagnetic scatter gun that accelerates a cloud of ferromagnetic micro-projectiles through a wide-bore magnetic barrel, creating a cone of hypersonic metal fragments that shreds soft targets and overwhelms personal armor through sheer volume of impacts. The SF-2 does not fire a single projectile — it fires approximately 1,200 needle-thin ferro-ceramic slivers per trigger pull, each one traveling at Mach 2.

The Scatterfield uses a disposable cassette system rather than conventional ammunition. Each cassette contains pre-packed ferromagnetic slivers suspended in a stabilizing gel that vaporizes during acceleration, ensuring uniform distribution across the cone of fire. The electromagnetic barrel requires a capacitor bank that takes 1.8 seconds to recharge between shots — an eternity in close combat that has driven operators to carry multiple SF-2 units rather than wait for recharge.

Arcturus developed the Hornets Nest as a counter-swarm weapon for engaging multiple light drones simultaneously. Its effectiveness against biological targets was, according to corporate communications, 'an emergent property of the platform's versatility.' The weapon's micro-projectiles lose lethal velocity beyond 20 meters, making it exclusively a close-range system — but within that range, nothing short of hardened plate armor offers meaningful protection.
specifications: projectile_count: ~1,200 ferro-ceramic slivers per cassette effective_range: 2-20 meters rate_of_fire: 1 shot per 1.8 seconds (capacitor recharge) capacity: 6-cassette rotary magazine weight: 4.1 kg with full magazine power_source: Integrated supercapacitor bank, 30 shots per charge cone_spread: 22 degrees at muzzle
tactical_use: Primarily deployed against drone swarms in enclosed environments where conventional firearms cannot engage fast-moving micro-targets effectively. The SF-2's wide cone of thousands of slivers creates an area denial effect that no small drone can navigate. Against personnel, the weapon is devastating at point-blank range but the recharge delay makes it a poor choice for sustained engagements. Experienced operators fire once and transition to a sidearm while the capacitor cycles.
cultural_context: Anti-drone warfare has become a daily reality in GLMZ's contested zones, and the Hornets Nest has given security teams a visceral, satisfying answer to the swarm problem. The sound of an SF-2 discharge — a sharp electromagnetic crack followed by the hissing impact of 1,200 slivers hitting everything downrange — has been described as 'angry static.' Drone operators have started calling contested corridors 'hive territory' when SF-2 units are known to be present.
story_hooks: Someone has modified SF-2 cassettes to contain chemically treated slivers that cause progressive tissue necrosis — turning a painful wound into a death sentence over 72 hours.
A drone operator has developed a swarm formation that can absorb SF-2 fire and continue its mission — the Hornets Nest's counter just became obsolete, and Arcturus is scrambling for a response.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, wide-muzzled scatter weapon with an aggressive forward-swept stance. The barrel flares dramatically at the terminus, resembling a predatory flower or insect mandible. Squat, muscular frame suggests contained explosive potential rather than graceful ballistics. Angular, asymmetrical geometry prioritizes function over elegance.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 58 cm | Width at muzzle: 12 cm | Height (including feed mechanism): 16 cm | Barrel length: 22 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial but not unwieldy — 4.1 kg with full magazine distributes across a compact frame, making it feel dense and purposeful in two-handed grip. The rotary cassette assembly sits low in the frame, anchoring weight near the centerline for quick target acquisition.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite with internal electromagnetic lattice frame; wide-bore barrel of hardened steel with magnetic shielding coils embedded in the walls
physical_description.finish: Battleship-gray anodized steel with matte polymer accent surfaces. The barrel mouth shows characteristic scorch marks and micro-metal scoring from fer-ceramic sliver discharge. Supercapacitor housing has a subtle iridescent shimmer under light — evidence of electromagnetic flux dampening coating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary body, matte charcoal polymer grip frame, brass-colored capacitor terminals visible through port vents, occasional burnt orange/copper discoloration at barrel rim from thermal stress
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with aggressive cross-hatching, designed for gloved operation. The grip bulges at stress points and terminates in a paddle-style magazine release. Secondary grip points molded below the barrel for two-handed stance control.
distinctive_features: Flared wide-bore muzzle with radiating magnetic coil vanes visible as raised ridges
Rotary cassette magazine with six clearly labeled slots, each holding a translucent ferro-ceramic cassette visible through clear polymer backing
Status LED trio (power, charge, cassette status) mounted on the right side — typically glowing amber during charge cycle
Heat dissipation vents along the barrel in geometric pattern, showing minor discoloration from use
Electromagnetic field indicator strip on top of receiver — color-shifting material that intensifies during capacitor discharge
Tactile feedback notches on the magazine rotation mechanism
Arcturus Defense Solutions' stylized 'AD' monogram stamped (not engraved) on the grip — deliberately functional, no decoration
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo on left side of frame near safety selector. Serial plate mounted on underside of grip: 'SF-2/HORNETS NEST' followed by six-character alphanumeric code. Regulation stamp: 'LICENSED ANTI-DRONE PLATFORM — GLMZ AUTHORITY' in small print on barrel shroud.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained by working operators — no deep gouges, but visible micro-scratches on the polymer grip and burnished spots on the barrel from repeated handling. Light corrosion around cassette vents from metal micro-particles. Supercapacitor port shows faint electrical scoring from connector use. Weapon clean enough to function, marked enough to show field service.
